claims.text: Co-free FeNiCrMn is derived from equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi by removing Co.
The initial Co-free FeNiCrMn alloy is in a solidified solid-solution state.
The dynamic behavior of Co-free FeNiCrMn is governed by temperature-dependent dislocation mobility.
The dynamic behavior of Co-free FeNiCrMn is governed by strain-rate sensitivity.
Solid-solution strengthening and the absence of Co influence dislocation mobility and strain-rate sensitivity.
The absence of Co alters the local atomic environment in FeNiCrMn.
The absence of Co alters solute-dislocation interactions.
Changes in solute-dislocation interactions modify strain-rate sensitivity and the temperature-dependent mechanical response.
At lower temperatures, reduced thermal activation limits dislocation motion.
At higher strain rates, solute-drag effects become prominent.
Relative to equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi under identical conditions, Co-free FeNiCrMn will have lower strain-rate sensitivity.
Relative to equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi, Co-free FeNiCrMn will have higher low-temperature yield strength because of enhanced solid-solution strengthening.
At high temperatures, dynamic recovery may occur in Co-free FeNiCrMn.
At high temperatures, Co-free FeNiCrMn may have ductility comparable to equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi.
At high temperatures, Co-free FeNiCrMn will have lower strength than equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi.
The proposed hypothesis is bounded to strain rates from 10^-3 to 10^3 s^-1 and temperatures from 77 K to 800 K.
A controlled comparison should test Co-free FeNiCrMn and equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi at identical temperatures and strain rates while measuring yield strength, ductility, and strain-rate sensitivity.
The hypothesis is falsified if Co-free FeNiCrMn has higher strain-rate sensitivity or lower low-temperature yield strength than equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi.
